current_state: Mixed gateway_http and legacy_commit_service write ownership; no single proven canonical kernel boundary for event or write authority.

recommended_order.title: Establish canonical event write ownership
recommended_order.description: Choose a single authoritative runtime for event persistence and event log writes, then assign gateway modules only adapter/ingress roles where possible.
actions: Identify whether gateway/event_repository.js or runtime/kernel/commit-service/src/events/event_log.ts will act as canonical event persistence.
Stop any new gateway-local event persistence flows from mutating semantic event state in parallel with legacy commit-service event logs.
Preserve gateway routes as ingress points while migrating write semantics into a single canonical runtime.

recommended_order.title: Consolidate legacy commit-service persistence domains
recommended_order.description: Treat audit, artifact, and lineage writes as a single legacy kernel surface and decide whether to retain, refactor, or retire it as a canonical service.
actions: Map legacy commit-service write modules into one canonical persistence boundary or retire them from production route exposure.
Avoid keeping both gateway and legacy commit-service Postgres write owners for overlapping domains.

recommended_order.title: Migrate gateway repository and snapshot writes
recommended_order.description: Move gateway-side object, snapshot, and registry writes into the chosen canonical owner or downgrade them to transport adapters only.
actions: Refactor gateway/repository_store.js and gateway/snapshot_repository.js so they no longer own the canonical write semantics unless the gateway is the single canonical owner.
If gateway remains only ingress, route these operations through the canonical kernel boundary.

recommended_order.title: Isolate Qdrant and vector memory writes
recommended_order.description: Separate vector memory writes from canonical persistence and decide whether they remain gateway-side adapters or are moved to a dedicated kernel-managed memory authority.
actions: Classify gateway/checkpoint_authority.js, gateway/memory_authority.js, gateway/context_compression_authority.js, and gateway/qdrant_bootstrap.js as infrastructure mutation adapters, not source-of-truth owners.
Ensure runtime/kernel/workers/qdrant_projection_worker.py does not create a third conflicting canonical write owner.

recommended_order.title: Prove static mediation for route ownership
recommended_order.description: Use route handler evidence and reachable file graphs to show that gateway routes delegate to a single kernel boundary instead of owning mixed persistence semantics.
actions: Produce static evidence that gateway routes call a kernel adapter interface rather than directly mutating Postgres or Qdrant state.
If gateway routes continue to reach commit-service files in reachable graphs, treat that as a signal that the runtime boundary is still mixed.

notes: This order is based only on the available evidence set and treats gateway_http and legacy_commit_service as coexisting runtime surfaces. It does not assume a dedicated mediation artifact exists.
